chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Ishaq, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Zain al-Abidin (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, says: 'By My Honor, My Greatness, My Majesty, My Beauty, My Elevation, and the height of My station, if a servant gives preference to his desire over My desire, I will place his concern in his Hereafter, and make him self-sufficient in his heart, and restrain his provision for him, and I guarantee the heavens and the earth his sustenance, and the world will come to him while it is reluctant.'

key_terms.الرَّاغِمَةُ: Reluctant or unwilling (referring to the world)
key_terms.هَوَاءُ الْعَبْدِ: The servant's own desire or whim

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for prioritizing God's pleasure over one's own desires?
ai.summary: This hadith qudsi, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, elucidates the spiritual mechanics of *ikhlas* (sincerity), where prioritizing divine pleasure over personal whims triggers a divine guarantee of provision (*rizq*) and peace of mind. The phrase 'compelled the world to come to her' reflects the Shia scholarly understanding that such a servant attracts worldly benefits not through pursuit, but as a natural consequence of their elevated spiritual status, ensuring they remain detached despite their gains.
